turns.text: it's 3:23 and i literally just woke up so short version pls. in the new charting system how do i document a late entry vs an addendum. ruben's sheet doesn't cover it

Short version:

- Late entry: you're documenting care that happened earlier but wasn't charted. Enter it now, label it "late entry," and give the current date/time plus the date/time the event actually occurred. Only chart what you personally know.
- Addendum: you're adding info to an entry that's already signed. Don't edit or delete the original. Add a new linked note with the current date/time and the reason.

In both cases, no overwriting and no backdating. Exact button names vary by system and facility, so check your hospital's charting policy or the in-system help for where these live.
ok. do the downtime forms need to be scanned in after or just kept. pouring my cà phê sữa đá into the thermos rn so typing one handed

Usually they need to be scanned or entered, not just kept. Most facilities treat downtime paperwork as part of the legal record, so the typical routine is:

- Fill out the paper form completely (date, time, signature)
- After the system is back up, scan it into the record per your facility's process, or transcribe the info in and mark it as entered from downtime documentation
- Don't discard the originals until your policy says it's okay

The exact rule is set by your facility's downtime policy, so that's the final word. Want a quick checklist version to keep by your workstation?

Downtime form checklist:

- Complete every field: date, time, patient identifiers, signature
- Write legibly, no scribbling out (single line through errors, initial and date)
- Once the system is back up: scan or enter per policy
- If transcribing, note it was from downtime documentation and include the original times
- Keep the paper original until policy says it can go
- Not sure? Check the downtime policy before the shift ends

Have a smooth night.
